I need to analyze this problem using fundamental principles of chromatography since I'm not getting search results. Let me think through this logically:

In HPLC (High-Performance Liquid Chromatography), the column dead time (t0) is the time it takes for an unretained compound to pass through the column. It represents the time the mobile phase takes to travel through the column.

Column porosity refers to the fraction of the column volume that is accessible to the mobile phase. It's essentially the void space within the column.

If we increase the porosity of the column:
1. There will be more void space (more empty volume) within the column
2. The mobile phase will have more volume to travel through
3. With more volume to travel through, it will take longer for the mobile phase to pass through the column

Since the column dead time is the time it takes for the mobile phase to pass through the column, an increase in porosity would lead to an increase in column dead time.
